title: Pop tunes for Goodman and the weekly deadline
summary: Moonlight on the Ganges and Love Walked In, and writing against deadlines.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: going back and forth, because I think these things all serve a purpose in an interesting way.

Aside from doing things like "Superman" and "Benny Rides Again" that we talked about, you did arrangements of pop tunes. One of the best that I've heard was "Moonlight on the Ganges", as far as a piece of scoring. How did you feel about doing the other pop tunes? I heard a chart, for example, you did on "Love Walked In"--
(Side B of Tape 2 ended at this point. Transcript will continue with Tape 3.)
(Side A of Tape 3 begins at this point.)
--you more or less, I'm on salary, so I have to write two or three of these a week.
You had to, whether you felt like it or not.

I try never to do something that I can't get myself involved in, but sometimes that's not always possible and you have a deadline and you do it. I'm sure that a lot of it was that way. After a while though it got so that I couldn't hear one note going to another, it was too repetitive, too much of the same thing. I just had to stop it. That was panic for a couple of years.
